headline: WESTERN MONEY IS BACK: $18B INTO GOLD ETFs IN AUGUST — BIGGEST EUROPEAN MONTHLY INFLOW EVER, HOLDINGS RECORD 4,189T
snippet: The World Gold Council reported September 9 that gold-backed ETFs attracted $18 billion in August — the second-largest monthly inflow on record — as Western institutional capital re-engaged at scale for the first time in two years: Europe led with $7.9 billion (its largest month ever), North America added $7.7 billion, and Asia contributed $2 billion (its best since February). Total holdings rose 121 tonnes to an all-time high of 4,189 tonnes and AUM climbed 16% to $615 billion.

headline: FIRST MINING DRILLS 5.26 G/T AU OVER 19.55M AND 3.43 G/T OVER 28M — MIROIR ZONE EXPANDS AT DUPARQUET, QUEBEC
snippet: First Mining Gold Corp. (TSX: FF) released September 10 the first assays from its 2026 program at the Duparquet Gold Project in Quebec: DUP26-093 returned 5.26 g/t Au over 19.55m (including 7.58 g/t over 12.95m) and DUP26-096 returned 3.43 g/t Au over 28.0m, both targeting down-plunge extensions of the Miroir discovery — a newly-defined high-grade zone first identified in 2024 that is now expanding at depth and along strike within a 15,000m 2026 program.

headline: TECTONIC METALS: 30M AT 1.40 G/T AU AT CHICKEN MOUNTAIN, ALASKA — CORRIDOR PUSHED TO 300M DEPTH, MAIDEN RESOURCE Q1 2027
snippet: Tectonic Metals Inc. (TSXV: TECT) announced September 10 results from 15 holes at Chicken Mountain, Flat Gold Project, Alaska: CMD26-036 returned 30m at 1.40 g/t Au (including 4.58 g/t over 4.50m) and 118m at 0.51 g/t Au, extending the higher-grade corridor to 300m vertical depth. Step-out holes 1.2km south expanded the southern drilled footprint by 200m to approximately 600m; 97 additional holes representing 18,000m of 2026 drilling remain pending assay ahead of a Q1 2027 maiden resource estimate.

headline: GOLD X2: 173M AT 0.89 G/T AU 100M BELOW THE QES PIT — ONTARIO'S MOSS GOLD PROJECT GROWS TO 6.7MOZ
snippet: Gold X2 Mining Inc. (TSXV/NYSE American: AUXX) released September 10 the latest results from its QES resource expansion program at the Moss Gold Project in Ontario: hole MQD-26-474 intersected 173m at 0.89 g/t Au from 685m depth (within 271.6m at 0.73 g/t from 630m), including 8m at 4.86 g/t, while MQD-26-465 returned 157.75m at 0.90 g/t. The program is extending a resource now at 2.46Moz Indicated (1.04 g/t) and 4.21Moz Inferred (0.97 g/t) with 12 of 21 planned deep holes complete.

headline: INVESTOR DEMAND DOUBLES IRRUPTIVE METALS' RAISE TO C$60M — BOUGHT DEAL CLOSES FOR CHILE'S PIMENTÓN COPPER-GOLD
snippet: Irruptive Metals Corp. (TSXV: IRR) closed a C$60 million bought deal private placement on September 10, issuing 48 million units at C$1.25 each with half-warrants at C$1.65 for 24 months. The raise launched at $30 million in August, upsized to $50 million on strong institutional book demand, and closed at $60 million after underwriters exercised their full over-allotment option — proceeds advancing Pimentón, a copper-gold exploration project in Chile.

headline: ALL 85 LANGIS TAILINGS HOLES HIT SILVER — BRIXTON METALS AVERAGES 61.7 G/T ACROSS 119.5M IN HISTORIC COBALT, ONTARIO CAMP
snippet: Brixton Metals Corp. (TSXV: BBB) reported September 8 that every hole in its maiden 85-hole sonic drill tailings characterization program at the Langis Silver Project in Cobalt, Ontario returned silver grades averaging 61.7 g/t on a length-weighted basis across 119.5m of tailings intersected, with individual drill holes as high as 810 g/t Ag — establishing consistent recoverable mineralization across the tailings footprint of a historic camp that produced over 600 million ounces of silver from 1906 to 1989.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACT CRACKS RECORD $96/LB — AI POWER DEMAND 'REMOVES THE CEILING' ON NUCLEAR
snippet: A September 10 analysis argues uranium remains structurally underpriced: the long-term contract price has reached a nominal record of $96/lb, exceeding the previous 2007 high of $95/lb, while spot holds near $89.60 — up roughly 10% year to date. TD Cowen projects global uranium demand rising from 205 million pounds in 2026 to 322 million pounds by 2035, against a projected 42-million-pound supply deficit, with AI data center buildout accelerating the timeline as tech companies lock in nuclear baseload via long-term PPAs.

headline: COPPER TARIFF 'STALL' OUTRUNS THE PAPER TRAIL — COPPER TRADERS SOLD 5% ON AN ANONYMOUS SOURCE, NOT A POLICY
snippet: A September 10 analysis argues that the Reuters report that sparked a 5%+ copper selloff — citing anonymous White House 'sources' saying the January 2027 copper tariff plan has stalled on affordability concerns — lacks any official support: no written policy document, administration statement or named official has confirmed a change to the tariff schedule. The analysis cautions that copper traders who exited the record-high trade on a single-source claim may have reacted to an assertion rather than a verified policy shift.

headline: CHILE AND PERU SUPPLY FEARS THAT DROVE COPPER TO $14,858/T AREN'T GOING AWAY — TARIFF DRAMA DOESN'T FIX MINES
snippet: A September 9 copper markets analysis notes that the supply-side drivers behind copper's record run — ongoing output disruptions at Codelco and delayed Peruvian expansion projects, combined with strong Chinese smelter demand — remain structural tailwinds entirely independent of US tariff policy. With Chilean mine output running below plan for the third straight year and no major greenfield projects ramping in the near term, the supply squeeze that underpinned $14,858/t copper is not resolved by tariff headlines.

headline: GOLDSEEK: 'WE'RE BULLISH' ON GOLD, SILVER AND COPPER — PPI ANXIETY MASKS THE INTACT STRUCTURAL DEMAND CASE
snippet: GoldSeek's latest market update maintains a bullish stance across gold, silver, and copper despite the August PPI print pushing September Fed rate-hike odds to 70%, arguing the structural supply-demand case for all three metals is intact and that near-term rate anxiety is creating a re-entry opportunity rather than an exit signal. The analysis points to gold holding above $4,380 through the PPI selloff — and Western ETF buyers absorbing $18 billion in August alone — as evidence that structural demand is now large enough to cushion paper-market selling.
